title: GeoChart Inputs Schema
description: This Schema validator validates the GeoChart Inputs.

title.description: Optionally provide the title of the Chart.

query.description: Optionally provide information on how the data should be queried in the table source. When undefined, the data has to be manually provided via datasources[].items values.

type.description: Indicate the kind of query to perform.

url.description: Indicate the url where to fetch the data to build the Chart with - supported urls are Esri services, OGC API Features services or urls pointing to a .json file built on the GeoJson format.

queryOptions.description: Query parameters to be used when querying the url.

whereClauses.description: Indicate how to generate the where clause to fetch the correct data in the table source. This is an array to support filtering on more than 1 field. The 'and' logic operator is implicit.

field.description: Indicate the field name, in the table source, on which to filter.

prefix.description: Indicate the prefix to use to build the query (useful to support single-quotes when the attribute to query is a string).

valueIs.description: Indicate the value as a literal information (not read from a property name from the datasource).

valueFrom.description: Indicate the property name, in the datasource.sourceItem(!), to dynamically read and provide to the query parameters in order to query the table source as indicated by the url.

suffix.description: Indicate the suffix to use to build the query (useful to support single-quotes when the attribute to query is a string).

orderByField.description: Optionally indicate the property on which to order the results of the data coming from the table source.

geochart.description: Groups information on how to build the Chart.

xAxis.description: Groups information on the X axis.

property.description: Indicate the property name on which to read the information from the table source.

grid.description: Grid options on linear graphs. For more grid options, refer to: https://www.chartjs.org/docs/latest/samples/scale-options/grid.html

display.description: Indicate if the grid lines should be displayed for the X axis. This option also removes the tick lines on the axis.

drawOnChartArea.description: Indicate if the grid lines should be displayed on the chart area. This option leaves the tick lines on the axis.

timeFormat.description: Defines the format string(s) used to display or parse time values. Can be a single format string (e.g., 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss') or an object with locale-specific format strings keyed by language code (e.g., { "en": "MMM dd, yyyy, HH:mm", "fr": "d MMM yyyy, HH:mm" }). Uses standard date formatting tokens (e.g., from date-fns or equivalent). Defaults to 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss' if not specified.

timeIANA.description: Specifies the IANA time zone identifier (e.g., 'America/Toronto', 'UTC') used for formatting and interpreting time values. Must be a valid time zone from the IANA Time Zone Database.

ticksRule.description: The rule to apply to provide the X axis ticks. 'auto' automatically calculates the optimal ticks on the axis. 'data' uses the actual data values to set the optimal ticks on the axis.

label.description: Indicate the label that should be shown for the axis.

usePalette.description: Optionally indicate a pre-determined (GeoChart specific) color palette should be used.

paletteBackgrounds.description: Optionally indicate an array of rgba color values to use as the palette for background coloring.

paletteBorders.description: Optionally indicate an array of rgb color values to use as the palette for border coloring.

yAxis.description: Groups information on the Y axis.

property.description: Indicate the property name on which to read the information from the table source.

grid.description: Grid options on linear graphs. For more grid options, refer to: https://www.chartjs.org/docs/latest/samples/scale-options/grid.html

display.description: Indicate if the grid lines should be displayed for the X axis. This option also removes the tick lines on the axis.

drawOnChartArea.description: Indicate if the grid lines should be displayed on the chart area. This option leaves the tick lines on the axis.

label.description: Indicate the label that should be shown for the axis.

usePalette.description: Optionally indicate a pre-determined (GeoChart specific) color palette should be used.

paletteBackgrounds.description: Optionally indicate an array of rgba color values to use as the palette for background coloring.

paletteBorders.description: Optionally indicate an array of rgb color values to use as the palette for border coloring.

tooltipSuffix.description: Optionally indicate the suffix to use on for the values when displayed in the Chart tooltip.

borderWidth.description: Optionally indicate the thickness of the borders (or lines in the line Chart).

useSteps.description: Optionally indicate if the line Chart should use steps.

tension.description: Optionally indicate if the Chart should use tension when drawing the line between the values (only possible with a line type Chart).

category.description: Optionally indicate how the data from the table source should be categorized (this creates the datasets aka the legend).

property.description: Indicate the property name to use to categorize records.

usePalette.description: Optionally indicate a pre-determined (GeoChart specific) color palette should be used.

paletteBackgrounds.description: Optionally indicate an array of rgba color values to use as the palette for background coloring.

paletteBorders.description: Optionally indicate the array of rgb color values to use as the palette for border coloring.

datasources.description: Groups information on the datasources to build the datasource drop down and the Chart.

display.description: Indicate the string to be displayed in the drop down.

sourceItem.description: Optionally indicate the source item(!) used when fetching the data using the 'query.url'. The source items represent the features loaded in the drop down. This property has an object with a property that should equal the property in 'query.queryOptions.whereClauses.valueFrom'.

value.description: Optionally indicate the inner value used for the 'sourceItem' - when 'display' alone isn't sufficient to distinguish the values.

items.description: Optionally indicate the actual items used to build the Chart. When a query.url is specified, the items will be fetched automatically. When items are specified/populated, the data isn't fetched via the 'query.url'.

ui.description: Optionally indicate what UI elements to show alongside the Chart.

xSlider.description: Groups information on the X axis slider.

display.description: Indicate if the slider on the X axis should be displayed.

step.description: Optionally indicate the steps the slider should jump when sliding.

min.description: Optionally indicate the minimum value for the slider.

max.description: Optionally indicate the maximum value for the slider.

ySlider.description: Groups information on the Y axis slider.

display.description: Optionally indicate if the slider on the Y axis should be displayed

step.description: Optionally indicate the steps the slider should jump when sliding.

min.description: Optionally indicate the minimum value for the slider.

max.description: Optionally indicate the maximum value for the slider.

stepsSwitcher.description: Optionally indicate if a drop down should be shown allowing to switch the steps on-the-fly.

scalesSwitcher.description: Optionally indicate if a drop down should be shown allowing to switch the scales on-the-fly.

resetStates.description: Optionally indicate if the button to reset the states should be displayed.

description.description: Optionally indicate descriptive text to show at the bottom of the Chart.

download.description: Optionally indicate if a download button should be displayed.

chartjsOptions.description: Optionally indicate further ChartJS specific options to open the door to further customization when natively supported by ChartJS: https://www.chartjs.org/docs/latest/general/options.html
